subject.title: feat(queue): persist followup queues across gateway restarts

question: Should OpenClaw accept durable at-least-once recovery for pending follow-up queues, including persisted routing/session descriptors and a Doctor-only sidecar migration, as the core restart-recovery contract?
rationale: The patch changes durable state and channel delivery semantics; deciding whether the documented replay window and recovery boundary are acceptable requires maintainer product and ownership judgment beyond the supplied proof.

options.title: Accept the bounded recovery contract
options.body: Approve SQLite-backed at-least-once recovery after verifying the exact-head migration, restore, and multi-channel routing behavior.

options.title: Require a narrower persistence boundary
options.body: Keep recovery durable but reduce or redesign persisted execution descriptors before accepting the shared-state contract.

options.title: Defer to broader restart recovery work
options.body: Pause this PR if follow-up recovery must be designed together with drain-window and offline-arrival handling.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded recovery contract
recommendation.body: Approve SQLite-backed at-least-once recovery after verifying the exact-head migration, restore, and multi-channel routing behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The provided discussion and adjacent gateway-restart reference make this the strongest available routing signal, although direct history inspection was unavailable.
